subject: Patient-reported dizziness on Calmerol - form attached
bodyText:
Dear Safety Team,

Please find attached a completed Patient Adverse Event Notification form for a patient
who called our pharmacy this morning reporting dizziness and mild nausea after starting
Calmerol three days ago.

I've filled in all the details we discussed with her over the phone in the attached PDF -
please refer to that for the full patient, product, and reaction information.

Kind regards,
James Okoro, PharmD
Oakridge Community Pharmacy

classifications.reason: A pharmacist reported a patient experiencing dizziness and mild nausea after taking Calmerol.

summary.summaryText: This document is a completed digital-native Patient Adverse Event Notification form generated by Oakridge Community Pharmacy under reference number AER-2026-0129. The report was completed on August 20, 2026, by a pharmacist named James Okoro in the United Kingdom. It documents an adverse reaction experienced by a 34-year-old female patient identified by the initials M.D.T. The patient has a relevant medical history of seasonal allergies with no other known conditions. The suspect product in question is Calmerol, a fictional drug administered orally at a dose of 10 mg twice daily. The product treatment started on August 15, 2026, and was ongoing at the time of the report. The patient experienced persistent dizziness and mild nausea beginning on the third day of treatment. The reaction was categorized as non-serious, requiring outpatient care with no hospitalization. At the time of reporting, the reaction was ongoing, and the patient was advised to contact her prescribing physician. The pharmacist filled out the form based entirely on a direct phone call from the patient. No photo or physical product sample was provided with the report. The document explicitly notes that it is a synthetically generated fictional form for software testing purposes.
